Actions.Label: Have a proper chat
Say: The blue chickens have started following me around the yard. I pretend I'm annoyed, but I keep slowing down for them.
Marnie says the coop latch needs fixing. I said I'd do it yesterday. The latch is still winning.
Joja coffee tastes like burnt cardboard. I know because I've had enough of it to identify the cardboard.
Jas asked whether chickens dream. I told her probably about worms. She said that sounded lonely, so now I'm reconsidering.
I used to think a quiet morning meant something was wrong. Turns out it can just mean nobody needs anything yet.
The saloon was loud last night. I stayed for one drink, then went home before I found a reason to stay too long.
There's a little patch behind the coop where the grass grows unevenly. The chickens like it. I'm leaving it alone.
People keep asking whether I'm doing better. I never know what answer they want, so I ask how their day is instead.
I bought a new pair of boots. They squeak. Marnie says they'll stop. I'm starting to think she enjoys the squeaking.
Charlie pecked my sleeve this morning and then followed me for twenty minutes. Apparently I'm her chosen idiot.
Some days the whole valley feels like it knows my business. Other days it doesn't even notice if I skip breakfast.
I've been trying to cook more. The first omelette stuck to the pan so badly I nearly had to sell the pan.
Jas is learning to whistle. She's terrible at it. I told her that means she's practising properly.
There's a difference between being alone and being left alone. I didn't understand that until recently.
Your farm smells like wet soil after rain. That's a compliment. Don't make me say it twice.
I found an old Joja badge in a drawer. Didn't throw it away. Didn't keep it on purpose, either.
Marnie keeps leaving the good feed near the door so I don't have to ask. She thinks I haven't noticed.
The chickens know the sound of the feed tin. Half the time they hear it before I even pick it up.
I don't mind people dropping by when they give me a warning. A knock is nice. A surprise is a whole different event.
I've been sleeping better. Not every night. Don't go making a parade out of it.
There's a song on the radio that makes me think of the road out of town. I still haven't decided whether that's good.
Jas drew me as a chicken. Apparently my hair looks like feathers. I put it on the fridge.
I don't have much advice about starting over. I can tell you where the spare nails are, though.
The best part of fixing the coop was hearing the door close properly. A small sound. A satisfying one.
I made enough soup for three people. Marnie took a jar, Jas took a bowl, and I didn't have to eat it all week.

Actions.Label: A latch that won't stay shut

Steps.Narrate: The coop door keeps swinging open in the breeze. Shane has one hand on the latch and a screwdriver tucked behind her ear.

Steps.Say: I know. I know. It's a simple fix. I've fixed worse things with less equipment and considerably more swearing.
Except this one keeps catching. You pull it shut, it looks fine, then the wind comes along and makes a fool of it.
Marnie said she'd ask Robin. I told her I could manage. Now the chickens are having a committee meeting outside.
I don't want the whole ranch rearranged every time something small breaks. I can do one thing without making it everyone's problem.
Could you hold the door while I try it again? Not because I can't. Because the hinge is awkward. That's different.

Options.Label: Line the hinge up and try once more.

Steps.Say: Right. Hold it there. No, a little higher. There. ...Oh. That's actually it. Don't look so pleased.

Options.Label: Ask Robin for a second opinion.

Steps.Say: I hate that that's sensible. Fine. I'll ask her. You can tell her I said please, if you want to make it worse.
Absolutely not. They're already convinced they're in charge. I don't need them signing off on repairs.
There. It shuts. The chickens are offended, naturally. Thanks for staying while I made a five-minute job last half an hour.

Actions.Label: A morning without the saloon
Actions.Conditions: Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch1_{{NpcName}}, PLAYER_HEARTS Current {{NpcName}} 4, Fouky.CharacterInteract_COUNTER Talks_{{NpcName}} 6, !Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch2_{{NpcName}}

Steps.Narrate: Shane is sitting on an overturned feed bucket. A thermos rests beside her, still warm.

Steps.Say: I brought coffee from home. It's not good coffee, but it's mine. That's apparently enough to make me protective of it.
I used to go to the saloon because I didn't want to hear my own house being quiet. Then I stayed because leaving felt harder.
I'm not telling you I've got everything sorted. I'm telling you I made a different choice yesterday, and I remembered it this morning.
Marnie didn't ask where I'd been. She just put a plate in the oven. I nearly made a joke about it, then didn't.
There's a chair by the window at the ranch. I might sit there after work. Sounds boring. I think I want boring.

Options.Label: Boring can be a good thing.

Steps.Say: Yeah. A chair, a cup of coffee, nobody expecting me to turn into a better person before supper. I could get used to that.

Options.Label: You don't have to explain your choices to me.

Steps.Say: Good. Because I don't have a speech prepared. I barely have a sentence. But thanks.

Options.Label: Want company on the quiet days?

Steps.Say: Maybe. Don't show up with a marching band. Just... knock. I'll see how I feel.
I'll keep the thermos. Tomorrow too, probably. It's odd having a plan that only requires remembering to wash a mug.

Actions.Label: The coop at sunrise
Actions.Conditions: Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch2_{{NpcName}}, PLAYER_HEARTS Current {{NpcName}} 6, Fouky.CharacterInteract_COUNTER Talks_{{NpcName}} 10, !Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch3_{{NpcName}}

Steps.Narrate: The first light touches the blue coop. Shane is standing outside with a small paper bag, watching the chickens wake.

Steps.Say: I used to think a good day had to be earned by doing something impressive. The chickens have never heard of that rule.
They want feed, clean water, and a door that shuts. They don't care if I've had a clever thought or fixed my whole life.
Jas helped me paint a little sign. It says 'Blue Coop'. She wanted 'The Very Famous Blue Chicken Hotel'. We compromised.
I've started leaving the door open while I work nearby. They wander out, scratch around, and come back when they feel like it.
That sounds simple when I say it. I suppose it is. I didn't say it was easy.

Options.Label: The Very Famous Blue Chicken Hotel.

Steps.Say: You are not helping. ...Actually, Jas would love that. Fine. I'll let her paint it. I refuse to be responsible for the spelling.
Yeah. It's ours. It doesn't need to sound important.

Options.Label: Leave it blank and let the chickens decide.

Steps.Say: They'd scratch a hole in it. Then we'd have a sign that says nothing. Very official.
Take the extra eggs. They're not payment. I just have more than I can use, and I know you won't let them go to waste.
